text: Stuffing your washing machine to the very top?
Your clothes are probably not getting clean. Here's why.
Inside the drum, small ridges called lifters pick up your clothes and drop them back into the water.
That tumbling, again and again, is what actually washes them.
In an overloaded drum, there is no room to fall.
The laundry turns as one big block, and the clothes in the middle barely get washed or rinsed.
A heavy, uneven load pulls to one side, and over time that strains the bearings and the shock absorbers.
The simple rule many manufacturers give: leave about a hand's width of space above your laundry.
